title: Assessing Long-Term Power Outage Preparedness in Sub-Threshold Enterprises Handling Hazardous Substances: Development and Pilot Application of the S-TERM-PO Framework
content: Long-term power outages can impair safety critical functions in facilities handling hazardous substances and may challenge the ability to maintain, achieve, and restore safe technological conditions. Building on the previously developed Sub-Threshold Enterprise Risk Management (S-TERM) method, this study develops the S-TERM Long-Term Power Outage Preparedness Framework (S-TERM-PO), a screening level approach for assessing preparedness in enterprises handling hazardous substances below the applicable qualifying quantities of Directive 2012/18/EU. The framework evaluates technical, organizational, procedural, and personnel capabilities required to maintain process safety during long-term outage of external electrical power. It comprises seven assessment domains assessed through a 48 assessment criteria checklist using a three level ordinal scale and a non-compensatory critical vulnerability rule. The framework was applied to four anonymized industrial facilities. Overall normalized preparedness scores ranged from 47.9% to 81.3%, corresponding to basic, moderate, and high preparedness classes. Domain level results showed that similar overall scores could conceal different preparedness profiles, particularly in emergency power, technological dependencies, and safe shutdown and restoration. The critical vulnerability rule identified four critical vulnerabilities in facility C and two in facility D, while none were identified in facilities A and B. The pilot application demonstrates the framework’s potential to identify preparedness gaps, preserve the visibility of process safety significant deficiencies, and support the prioritization of improvement measures, while further validation across broader industrial settings is required.
